description: Orchestration, seed corpus & QA — a job runner that drives many categories end-to-end (acquire -> normalize -> link -> export) with scheduling, incremental re-runs, a catalog, and quality gates, then proves the whole system by building a real multi-domain seed corpus (dishes, sculptures, monuments, battles, languages) and validating the resulting graph.

tasks.title: T6-US-001: Define a pipeline job model and config
tasks.description:
As a developer, I need to declare an end-to-end job so categories run reproducibly through every stage.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Define a Job config (one or more category specs, target stages: acquire/normalize/link/export, output paths)
- Jobs are declared in a jobs/<name>.yml and validated on load with clear errors
- A Job dataclass exposes the ordered stages to run
- Tests pass (pytest) loading valid and invalid job configs
- Type checks pass (mypy)

Project context: culture-scrape — see PLAN.md, docs/data-model.md, docs/prior-art.md. Work in the repo root (src/culturescrape/). This story belongs to tasklist 'ralph/orchestration-seedcorpus'.

tasks.title: T6-US-002: Implement the pipeline runner
tasks.description:
As a user, I want a single runner that chains acquire -> normalize -> link -> export so I don't wire stages by hand.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Runner executes the stages from US-001 in order, passing each stage's output dir to the next, calling the modules from Tasklists 1-5
- A stage failure stops that job with a clear error and a non-zero exit, leaving completed stage outputs intact
- Per-stage timing and row counts are recorded
- Tests pass (pytest) running a fixture job end-to-end with adapters mocked
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T6-US-003: Implement incremental / idempotent re-runs
tasks.description:
As a user, I want re-running a job to update only what changed so large corpora are cheap to refresh.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Each stage records an input fingerprint; a stage is skipped when inputs are unchanged unless --force is given
- Re-running an unchanged job performs no network calls and reports 'up to date'
- Updated source data triggers re-normalization and re-linking only for affected categories
- Tests pass (pytest) asserting a second run is a no-op and a changed input triggers re-processing
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T6-US-004: Run categories concurrently with backpressure
tasks.description:
As a user, I want many categories processed in parallel within polite limits so large corpora finish quickly.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Acquire stages for independent categories run concurrently up to a configurable worker cap
- Per-host rate limits from the acquisition client are respected across concurrent workers
- A failure in one category does not abort the others; a final summary lists per-category status
- Tests pass (pytest) running multiple fixture categories concurrently with a stubbed adapter
- Type checks pass (mypy)

tasks.title: T6-US-006: Implement quality gates
tasks.description:
As a user, I want automated QA so low-quality scrapes are flagged before they pollute the graph.

Acceptance criteria (all must be met before marking complete):
- Gates check: minimum row count vs expected, max duplicate rate post-dedup, provenance completeness, dangling-edge rate, and unreconciled-entity rate
- Each gate has a configurable threshold; violations are reported and (optionally) fail the run
- A QA report (JSON + printed summary) is written per job
- Tests pass (pytest) for a passing fixture and a fixture that trips each gate
- Type checks pass (mypy)
